statement: Build a catalogue of the app's functionality before combining the warrenghaad version with main.
rationale: The owner needs to see what each version does to merge them successfully.

statement: The same functionality catalogue approach should work across all of the owner's repositories and Replit projects.
The catalogue is presented like an eTextbook, built from the owner's Figma eTextbook file and Card Stack design.
Work in three tiers: a reusable template (Figma eTextbook + Card Stack), then a functionality catalogue built on it, then the ArtisanalCanvas catalogue.

Claude writes the considerations, specifications, prompts, skills, constraints, and cross-repo tools, and reviews the results; Replit does the build work (template import, card stack, catalogue screens, app entries and screenshots).
rationale: The owner doubts the Replit agent's ability to plan its own work, and the build work is straightforward.

statement: The tier 1 template is one combined Figma file (made by Claude through the Figma connector) plus a Storybook of built components linked to its frames.
Prism stays in the eventual integration scope, but is not built, and its workspace/row/column grid is not imposed, until the app's structure is inventoried and designed.
source: Recorded by the Replit agent in .agents/memory/prism-scope.md; consistent with task #12

statement: The drawing cube workspace uses real raster references only; no AI-generated, ASCII, or SVG visuals there.
source: Recorded by the Replit agent in .agents/memory/cube-contract.md

statement: Catalogue records live in this repository's catalogue/ folder; Replit memory and task files only point to them.
rationale: Replit's .agents and .local files are not in GitHub, so Claude, Codex, and other repos can't see them.

statement: Bring warrenghaad features into main one at a time, guided by the catalogue, instead of a git merge.
rationale: The two versions share no git history and differ in about 31,000 files.

statement: Replace Replit task #12 and the two paused catalogue tasks with the task sequence in catalogue/prompts/.
rationale: Task #12's operating brief, skills, and templates now exist in catalogue-kit/; the paused tasks jump to building UI before the template and pilot.
